what: Image Steganography hides a text message inside a picture. The picture looks the same, but the message is stored in the tiniest colour changes of its pixels (the lowest bit of red, green and blue). Reveal mode reads it back.

You can also lock the message with a password (AES-256-GCM, PBKDF2-SHA256 with 600,000 rounds), so even someone who knows a message is hidden cannot read it. A small header with the length and a checksum tells you if the picture was changed.
The result is always a PNG, because JPEG compression and apps that shrink photos destroy hidden messages. Everything runs on your device.
uses: Hide a birthday riddle or treasure-hunt clue inside a photo for friends.
Hide your name and date inside artwork you share as files.
See how much text a picture can hold and why compression breaks it.
Pass a note with a password
Hide a locked message so only the person with the password can read it.
tutorial: Click the box and choose a PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF or BMP. Bigger pictures hold more text; the line under the preview shows how much room there is.
Type the secret message. The counter shows how many bytes it uses and turns red if it does not fit.
Tick "Also lock the message with a password" and type it twice. Without it, anyone using a tool like this can read the message.
Press "Hide message". The tool checks the new picture really holds the message, then you press Download PNG.
Email it as an attachment, share it in a cloud drive, or use "send as document" in a chat app. Sending it as a photo would destroy the message.
Choose "Reveal a message" and pick the PNG. The message appears, or a password box if it is locked.
features: Width, height and how many bytes fit, updated as you type.
A CRC-32 checksum tells a damaged message apart from no message at all.
AES-256-GCM encryption with a strong password-based key.
PNG is lossless, so every hidden bit stays exactly as written.
The new picture is read back before you download it, to be sure the message is there.
If a picture was recompressed, it says so plainly instead of showing garbage.
Messages are stored as UTF-8, so Arabic, Chinese, Hindi and emoji all work.

example.title: Worked example: a clue in a holiday photo
example.text: Your photo beach.jpg is 1600 × 1200 pixels, so it has room for about 720,000 bytes. You type "The next clue is under the blue chair" and press Hide message. You download beach-hidden.png (about 3 MB, bigger than the JPG because PNG is lossless) and email it to your friend. They open Reveal a message, pick the PNG and read the clue. When they post the same picture on social media, the app recompresses it, and the message is gone, which is why you sent it as a file.

tips: Always share the PNG as a file or document, never as a photo in a chat or social app.
Do not edit, crop, resize or re-save the picture as JPEG after hiding a message.
Use a password if the message is private; hiding alone is not security.
Photos with lots of detail hide changes best, but any picture works.
Fully see-through pixels are skipped, so pictures with big transparent areas hold less.
problems: "No hidden message found" with a JPEG
JPEG compression destroys hidden messages. Ask for the original PNG file, sent as a document or attachment.
"A hidden message was found, but it is damaged"
The picture was changed after the message was hidden (recompressed, resized or edited). Get the original PNG.
"The message is too long for this picture"
Shorten the message or use a bigger picture.
Check the password, including capital letters. If it is right, the picture was changed.
